author: nickyeow

english.text: Would you please not leave the door open?

jyutping: nei5 ho2 m4 ho2 ji5 m4 hou2 hoi1 zyu6 dou6 mun4 aa3？
text: 你可唔可以唔好開住道門呀？

author: nickyeow

english.text: I bought this T-shirt on sale.

jyutping: ngo5 maai5 zo2 ni1 gin6 gaam2 gan2 gaa3 ge3 T seot1。
text: 我買咗呢件減緊價嘅 T 恤。

author: nickyeow

english.text: Don't you feel the house shaking?

jyutping: nei5 m4 gok3 dak1 gaan1 uk1 hai2 dou6 zan3 gan2 me1？
text: 你唔覺得間屋喺度震緊咩？

author: nickyeow

english.text: By the way, I have something to tell you.

jyutping: hai6 laa3，ngo5 jau5 di1 je5 jiu3 waa6 nei5 zi1。
text: 係喇，我有啲嘢要話你知。

author: nickyeow

english.text: I am watering the flowers.

jyutping: ngo5 hai2 dou6 bong1 gan2 di1 faa1 lam4 seoi2。
text: 我喺度幫緊啲花淋水。

author: nickyeow

english.text: He stood up.

jyutping: keoi5 kei5 zo2 hei2 san1。
text: 佢企咗起身。

author: nickyeow

english.text: Can I have a few words with you?

jyutping: ho2 m4 ho2 ji5 tung4 nei5 king1 gei2 geoi3 aa3？
text: 可唔可以同你傾幾句呀？

author: kaenif

english.text: Your hair really does look untidy.

jyutping: nei5 di1 tau4 faat3 dou1 hou2 m4 zing2 cai4 bo3。
text: 你啲頭髮都好唔整齊噃。

author: kaenif

english.text: After you.

jyutping: nei5 sin1。
text: 你先。

author: nickyeow

english.text: He is still angry.

jyutping: keoi5 zung6 nau1 gan2。
text: 佢仲嬲緊。

author: tigro1973

english.text: Your excellent work puts me to shame.

jyutping: nei5 jat1 lau4 ge3 gung1 zok3 ling6 ngo5 gam2 dou3 caam4 kwai5。
text: 你一流嘅工作令我感到慚愧。

author: nickyeow

english.text: He is a bit like his father.

jyutping: keoi5 jau5 di1 ci5 keoi5 lou5 dau6。
text: 佢有啲似佢老豆。

author: nickyeow

english.text: The photos are taken by a pro, so they'll turn out well.

jyutping: di1 soeng2 hai6 zyun1 jip6 sip3 jing2 si1 jing2 ge3，so2 ji5 m4 wui5 jau5 man6 tai4。
text: 啲相係專業攝影師影嘅，所以唔會有問題。

author: nickyeow

english.text: Look! There is a cat in the kitchen.

jyutping: tai2 haa2！cyu4 fong2 dou3 jau5 jat1 zek3 maau1。
text: 睇吓！廚房到有一隻貓。

author: kaenif

english.text: He's not an idiot.

jyutping: keoi5 m4 hai6 so4 gaa3。
text: 佢唔係傻㗎。

author: nickyeow

english.text: I cannot have a nap at the office.

jyutping: ngo5 m4 ho2 ji5 hai2 baan6 gung1 sat1 dou3 fan3 aan3 gaau3。
text: 我唔可以喺辦公室到瞓晏覺。

author: nickyeow

english.text: There used to be a bridge there.

jyutping: go2 dou3 cang4 ging1 jau5 jat1 tiu4 kiu4。
text: 嗰到曾經有一條橋。

author: nickyeow

english.text: How long will this take?

jyutping: jiu3 gaau2 gei2 noi6 gaa3？
text: 要搞幾耐㗎？

author: nickyeow

english.text: It's not polite to point at others.

jyutping: sau2 zi2 zi2 mou5 lai5 maau6。
text: 手指指冇禮貌。

author: nickyeow

english.text: I've had too many disappointments.

jyutping: ngo5 ji5 ging1 sat1 mong6 gwo3 taai3 do1 ci3。
text: 我已經失望過太多次。

author: thesilhouette

english.text: "Is it already two?" "No, it's just five after one."

jyutping: gaap3 man6：「loeng5 dim2 laa3？」jyut3 daap3：「mei6，jat1 dim2 daap6 jat1 ze1。」
text: 甲問：「兩點喇？」乙答：「未，一點踏一啫。」

author: Davidgo5867

english.text: The human mind, no matter how highly trained, cannot grasp the universe. We are in the position of a little child, entering a huge library whose walls are covered to the ceiling with books in many different tongues. The child knows that someone must have written those books. It does not know who or how. It does not understand the languages in which they are written. The child notes a definite plan in the arrangement of the books, a mysterious order, which it does not comprehend, but only dimly suspects. That, it seems to me, is the attitude of the human mind, even the greatest and most cultured, toward God.

text: 人類嘅頭腦，無論訓練得幾高，都掌握唔到宇宙。我哋喺一個細路仔嘅位置，進入一個巨大嘅圖書館，圖書館嘅牆身覆蓋到天花板，上面有好多唔同語言嘅書。個小朋友知道嗰啲書一定係有人寫嘅，佢唔明白佢哋用嘅語言寫，個小朋友喺啲書嘅排列中記低咗一個明確嘅計劃，呢個係一個神秘嘅順序，佢唔明白，但係只係模糊噉懷疑，呢個係人類對上帝嘅態度，就算係最偉大同最有文化嘅人。

author: Davidgo5867

english.text: Some Japanese joke that I'm in "Liverpool." Many of them consider my English more British than American. I think that some Japanese fantasize marrying whites, as did my high school classmate Derek M. of Japanese ancestry. English is something that Japanese now learn from about Grade 5, age 10. But I think that English in Japan is something like French in BC. The English are looked upon as a highly progressive group, despite being known for being snooty or even rude. If people knew me, they would know that I find more wealth in learning Australian Aboriginal languages or Amerindian languages. I have a different view of "wealth" from other people. I find more enjoyment in Latino languages such as Spanish, French, Portuguese, Catalan, Italian, Chabacano, Esperanto, and Interlingua, all of which I do know in varying degrees. English is not my preference, as I do find it ordinary. I delve into Orientalism, as Japanese, Korean, Chinese, Thai, and Vietnamese. Esperanto and Lojban increasingly encapsulate my varied rainbow interests of the East and West.

text: 有啲日本人講笑話我喺「利物浦」。佢哋當中好多人覺得我嘅英文係英式多過美式。我覺得有啲日本人幻想同白人結婚，我高中同學 Derek M. 都係咁。英文係日本人而家大約五年級，10歲嗰陣學嘅嘢。但我覺得日本嘅英文同公元前嘅法文有啲似。英國人被視為一個高度進步嘅群體，儘管佢哋出名係傲慢甚至粗魯。如果人哋識我，佢哋就會知道我喺學習澳洲原住民語言或者美洲印第安人語言方面搵到更多財富。我對「財富」嘅睇法同其他人唔同。我喺拉丁裔語言入面搵到更多享受，例如西班牙文、法文、葡萄牙文、加泰羅尼亞文、意大利文、查巴卡諾文、世界語同間語言，我確實識得唔同程度。英文唔係我嘅偏好，因為我覺得佢普通。我深入研究東方主義，例如日本人、韓國人、香港人、中國人、泰國人同越南人。世界語同洛伊班越嚟越包含我對東西方嘅多元化彩虹興趣。

author: Davidgo5867

english.text: Long, long ago, there lived an old man and an old woman; they were peasants, and had to work hard to earn their daily rice. The old man used to go and cut grass for the farmers around, and while he was gone the old woman, his wife, did the work of the house and worked in their own little rice field.

text: 好耐好耐之前，嗰度住咗一個老人同一個老婆；佢哋係農民，要努力工作先可以賺到佢哋日常嘅飯。老細成日去幫周圍嘅農夫割草，而當佢唔喺度嘅時候，老婆，即係佢老婆，做咗間屋嘅工作，同埋喺佢哋自己嘅細稻田度做嘢。
